title: Extra-coordinate homotopy on continuous cochains of a split topological map
statement:
Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $T,V$ be topological spaces, $q:T\to V$ a continuous map, $\sigma:V\to T$ continuous with $q\sigma=\mathrm{id}_V$, and $A$ an abelian group with a topology for which addition and negation are continuous. For $r\geq1$, put $T_V^r=\{(t_0,\ldots,t_{r-1})\in T^r:q(t_i)=q(t_j)\text{ for all }i,j\}$ with the subspace topology. For $n\geq0$ let $C^n=C(T_V^{n+1},A)$ be the additive group of all continuous functions, with
$$(d^nf)(t_0,\ldots,t_{n+1})=\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(-1)^jf(t_0,\ldots,\widehat{t_j},\ldots,t_{n+1}),$$
where a minus sign denotes additive inversion. For every $n\geq1$ the rule
$$(h_nf)(t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1})=f(\sigma(q(t_0)),t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1})$$
defines an additive map $h_n:C^n\to C^{n-1}$ and satisfies
$$d^{n-1}(h_nf)+h_{n+1}(d^nf)=f\qquad(f\in C^n).$$
The statement includes $n=1$ and empty $T,V$; no compactness, separation, metrizability or completeness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Write $X_r=T_V^r$ for $r\geq1$. Deleting coordinate $j$ gives $p_j:X_{r+1}\to X_r$: every pair of retained coordinates still has equal $q$-image. Set $s_r(x)=(\sigma(q(x_0)),x_0,\ldots,x_{r-1})$. Since $q\sigma(q(x_0))=q(x_0)=q(x_i)$, this tuple belongs to $X_{r+1}$. These are actual maps of the displayed tuple spaces, without choosing any point of $T$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written split-cover auxiliary, explicit coordinate proof, step 1

proof.text: Both maps are continuous directly from the topologies. The inverse image under $p_j$ of a coordinate-open cylinder is a coordinate-open cylinder in $X_{r+1}$. For $s_r$, a cylinder in coordinate zero pulls back to $\{x:x_0\in(\sigma\circ q)^{-1}(U)\}$, open since $q,\sigma$ are continuous; a cylinder in coordinate $i+1$ pulls back to $\{x:x_i\in U\}$. Product opens are unions of finite intersections of cylinders; subspace opens are their intersections with $X_r$. Thus these calculations prove continuity into the indicated subspaces.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written split-cover auxiliary, explicit coordinate proof, step 2

proof.text: Continuous functions into $A$ are closed under pointwise zero, addition and negation: for example $(f+g)^{-1}(U)=(f,g)^{-1}(+^{-1}(U))$, and the pair map is continuous by inverse images of open rectangles. Composition is continuous because inverse images compose. Hence $d^n$ is well-defined as a finite signed sum of $f\circ p_j$, and $h_n(f)=f\circ s_n$ is continuous. Pointwise, $h_n(f+g)=h_n(f)+h_n(g)$ and $h_n(0)=0$, proving additivity.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written split-cover auxiliary, explicit coordinate proof, step 3

proof.text: For clarity write $p_j^{(r)}:X_{r+1}\to X_r$ for deletion of coordinate $j$. For $x=(t_0,\ldots,t_n)\in X_{n+1}$ with $n\geq1$, put $a=\sigma(q(t_0))$. Coordinatewise, $p_0^{(n+1)}s_{n+1}(x)=x$ and $p_{j+1}^{(n+1)}s_{n+1}(x)=s_n(p_j^{(n)}x)$ for $0\leq j\leq n$. For $j>0$ the first retained $t$-entry is $t_0$; for $j=0$ it is $t_1$, and $\sigma(q(t_1))=a$ because $q(t_1)=q(t_0)$. The remaining entries agree in order. The condition $n\geq1$ ensures $t_1$ exists and $s_n$ is defined.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written split-cover auxiliary, explicit coordinate proof, step 4

proof.text:
Expanding the definitions at $x$ and using step 4 gives
$$ (d^{n-1}h_nf)(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}(-1)^j f(s_n(p_j^{(n)}x)),\qquad
(h_{n+1}d^nf)(x)=f(x)+\sum_{j=0}^{n}(-1)^{j+1} f(s_n(p_j^{(n)}x)). $$
Set $b_j=(-1)^j f(s_n(p_j^{(n)}x))$. The corresponding term of the second sum is $-b_j$: the two exponents have opposite parity. Commutativity and associativity rearrange the sum of both displayed expressions as $f(x)+\sum_{j=0}^{n}(b_j+(-b_j))=f(x)$; each pair is zero. Equality at every tuple proves the required equality of continuous functions.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written split-cover auxiliary, explicit coordinate proof, step 5

proof.text: For $n=1$, the two expressions are $f(a,t_1)-f(a,t_0)$ and $f(t_0,t_1)-f(a,t_1)+f(a,t_0)$, so the same cancellation includes the lowest degree. If $T$ is empty, the given section forces $V$ empty; conversely a map $T\to\varnothing$ forces $T$ empty. All $X_r$ are then empty, each $C^n$ is the one-element group, and the identity is automatic. No step used separation, compactness, a metric, or completeness.
